findings.title: deleteMany retryCount condition is not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The second branch of the OR clause in the deleteMany call (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` restriction, unlike the first branch. Since `retryCount` is a generic field on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model (also used, e.g., by `WebhookScheduledTriggers`-like retry concepts, or potentially by future email/WhatsApp retry logic), any WorkflowReminder row of any method that ends up with retryCount > 1 will be permanently deleted by this SMS-specific cron endpoint, even if it is an EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder unrelated to SMS sending. This can cause unintended data loss for non-SMS reminders if retryCount is ever incremented elsewhere, and is inconsistent with the stated intent of only cleaning up failed SMS reminders.

findings.title: Catch block treats all errors as SMS send failures, risking premature deletion
findings.body: The try block spans many operations beyond the actual SMS send: fetching the organizer's profile, resolving the booker URL, parsing booking metadata, rendering templates, etc. Any exception from these unrelated operations (e.g., a transient DB query failure, a template rendering bug, or a metadata parsing error) is caught by the same catch block and increments `retryCount` exactly like a genuine SMS delivery failure (e.g., invalid phone number). Combined with the new deletion logic (retryCount > 1 triggers deletion), two unrelated/transient errors on a reminder are enough to have it permanently deleted, even though the actual SMS send may never have been attempted or may have been perfectly deliverable. This conflates infrastructure/transient errors with the specific 'invalid phone number'-type failures the PR intends to handle, risking silent loss of valid reminders.

findings.title: No retry/cleanup path when message or sendTo is empty
findings.body: When `message` is falsy/empty or `sendTo` is missing, the code silently does nothing (no retryCount increment, no scheduling, no logging). Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` indefinitely and are only ever cleaned up once their `scheduledDate` passes (via the first deleteMany branch), meaning they can linger unprocessed for up to 7 days without any retryCount-based accounting or visibility, unlike the newly added failure paths. This inconsistency was not addressed by this PR despite being a closely related failure mode (e.g., a booking never had a phone number set).

findings.title: Missing test coverage for new retryCount/deletion behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces non-trivial new behavior (incrementing retryCount on failure, and deleting reminders once retryCount exceeds 1) but no tests were added or updated to verify: (1) retryCount increments correctly on both the 'no scheduledSMS result' path and the exception path, (2) the deleteMany call actually removes reminders with retryCount > 1, and (3) it does not inadvertently remove unrelated reminders. Given this logic directly affects whether customer-facing SMS reminders get silently dropped, the lack of test coverage is a notable gap for a bug-fix PR.
